subject: Service degradation & ledger adjustment request — proposed path and contract sequencing
messages:
From: David Chen <david.chen@vectra.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: support@vectra.ai
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service degradation — request for billing adjustment

Karthik,

Thanks for the quick acknowledgement on the outage this morning. Our production traffic saw a sustained latency increase (p50 moved from ~120ms to ~850ms) between 03:20–08:05 PDT and some 5xx errors for a subset of inference requests. That window materially impacted our transaction rate and downstream SLAs with our customers.

We need Redwood to: 1) confirm the root-cause timeline, 2) provide the calculated impact on our monthly usage, and 3) propose a ledger adjustment (service credit or refund) to reconcile the hours we were degraded. Because this is hitting our revenue targets we also want executive visibility — can you set up an exec call tomorrow?

Attached: csv extract of our error-rate spikes and sample request IDs.

Appreciate urgency — David

--
David Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, Vectra AI
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: David Chen <david.chen@vectra.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service degradation — request for billing adjustment

David — thanks for the note and the CSV; sorry for the impact. I’m escalating this inside Redwood and will get you: a concise incident timeline, an impact calculation (tokens and requests affected), and a proposed ledger adjustment by EOD tomorrow.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- I’ll pull the server-side request logs and cross-reference with your sample request IDs (LA by 13:00 PDT).
- Lauren (finance) will draft a preliminary invoice adjustment and compensation formula.
- Ben (sales/CS) will join the exec call to align commercial framing.

We can do an executive touchpoint tomorrow at 11:00 PDT — does that work for you? If yes, I’ll send an invite and include our incident lead and finance.

Attachments: — I’ve uploaded your CSV to our incident workspace and attached the incident timeline stub we’re starting to fill.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service degradation — request for billing adjustment

Karthik / Ben — I reviewed the early telemetry. If the affected window is ~4.7 hours and ~18% of Vectra’s hourly throughput during that window failed or was degraded, a typical commercial approach would be:

- Option A (credit): pro-rate the impacted token-hours equivalent at 1.25x to account for downstream SLA exposure.
- Option B (refund): apply a one-time invoice credit equal to the pro-rated impacted usage (no multiplier).

For anything over $50k we need VP approval; anything below I can sign off. Given Vectra’s ARR and the revenue at risk, we should prepare the VP note and a short justification. Ben — pls confirm whether this should be positioned as a MakeWhole credit vs. contractual SLA credit.

I’ll draft the invoice adjustment PDF (proposed_invoice_adjustment_v1.pdf) and attach.

— Lauren Bishop
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service degradation — request for billing adjustment

Lauren — thanks. Position as SLA contractual credit first; Vectra will appreciate an explicit SLA amendment path (we can add language that clarifies quantification and timing for remediation credits). For the exec call, I’ll take the commercial part and highlight the ongoing mitigation steps we’ve put in place (routing policies, temporary capacity bump).

Proposed negotiation stance:
- Start with Option A (1.25x credit) in the first offer.
- If Vectra pushes, move to Option B but propose a one-time committed capacity uplift (2 weeks of burst capacity at no charge) as an alternative.
- Offer a dedicated post-incident performance review with engineering and product.

Rishi — I’ve included you to make sure the entitlement logic is correct for their contract and to check whether there are any platform exceptions that would change the calculation.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: David Chen <david.chen@vectra.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 16:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service degradation & ledger adjustment request — proposed path and contract sequencing

David — thank you again for the patience and the data you shared. We value the partnership and want to be practical and fast. Here’s our proposed path ahead: 

Summary of factual items:
- Impact window: 2026-08-18 03:20 PDT through 2026-08-18 08:05 PDT (as matched across our logs and your samples).
- Estimated affected usage: ~17.9% of requests in that window; our preliminary token-hour calc attached.

Commercial proposal (initial offer) — please review before our exec call, scheduled 11:00 PDT tomorrow: 
1) SLA credit: pro-rated service credit equal to impacted usage * 1.25 multiplier applied to August invoice (appears as a negative line item).
2) Operational remediation: two-week capacity uplift (no charge) to cover burst windows while we complete the routing fixes.
3) Contract sequencing: we’ll add a one-paragraph amendatory note to the SOW that documents the incident and the crediting approach; this will be signed post-acceptance.

Attachments: proposed_invoice_adjustment_v1.pdf (draft figures), incident_timeline_20260819.csv (matching request IDs you provided).

If this is acceptable as a starting point we’ll escalate for internal VP approval today and circulate a formal amendment and credit memo by EOD Monday. 

Call invite coming now.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
